2027-04-29.title: Thursday of the fourth week after Qyomtho · St Catherine of Siena
readings: May the God of peace sanctify you entirely; the one who calls you is faithful
The wise and foolish bridesmaids: “Look! Here is the bridegroom!”
2027-04-29.alt: Season of Qyomtho (the Resurrection), the week after the Fourth Sunday after Qyomtho. The Panchangam remembers St Catherine of Siena, virgin and Doctor of the Church.
2027-04-29.verse: The one who calls you is faithful, and he will do this.
theo: The Gospel today is a wedding story, and it suits the saint the Church remembers. In Jesus' time the bridegroom came at night to bring his bride home, and young women of the village waited with lamps to light the procession. “Ten bridesmaids took their lamps and went to meet the bridegroom. Five of them were foolish, and five were wise.” The difference is small and decisive: “the wise took flasks of oil with their lamps.” The bridegroom is delayed; all of them sleep. “But at midnight there was a shout, ‘Look! Here is the bridegroom! Come out to meet him.’” The lamps of the foolish are going out, and oil cannot be borrowed at the last moment. While they go to buy it, “the bridegroom came, and those who were ready went with him into the wedding banquet; and the door was shut.” Jesus ends: “Keep awake therefore, for you know neither the day nor the hour.” St Augustine asked what the oil is, and answered that it is charity, the love that is not seen from outside but keeps the lamp burning; no one can lend another his love at the door (Sermon 93, in substance). St Ephrem and the Syriac Fathers loved to call Christ the Bridegroom and the Church his bride; in this Qyomtho season we know him as the risen Bridegroom, and he will come again. Is there oil in our lamps?

St Paul's blessing for the Thessalonians reads like a prayer for wise bridesmaids: “May the God of peace himself sanctify you entirely; and may your spirit and soul and body be kept sound and blameless at the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ.” Holiness is not only for the soul; the whole person, spirit, soul and body, is to be made ready for the Lord. That is why the Church cares for the body as well as the soul: in fasting and feasting, in chastity, in caring for the sick. Then comes the sentence that removes our fear: “The one who calls you is faithful, and he will do this.” We do not fill our lamps by our own strength. God who calls is faithful; he keeps pouring the oil of his grace through prayer and the sacraments, if we keep coming back for it. And Paul adds two very human requests: “Beloved, pray for us. Greet all the brothers and sisters with a holy kiss.” Holiness is never private. It grows in a community that prays for one another and shares the peace, as we do at the Qurbono when the kiss of peace passes from the altar through the whole church.

St Catherine of Siena was such a wise virgin. Born in 1347, one of the youngest of some twenty-five children of a dyer's family, she gave her life to Christ while still a girl and later joined the Dominican lay sisters of her city, the Mantellate. She nursed the sick in times of plague, visited prisoners, and gathered around her a circle of disciples. Though she had little schooling, she dictated a great book of spiritual teaching, the Dialogue, and some three hundred and eighty of her letters survive. With bold love she wrote to princes and to the Pope himself, and in 1376 she travelled to Avignon to beg Pope Gregory XI to return to Rome; he did so the next year. She died in Rome on 29 April 1380, at the age of thirty-three. Pope Paul VI declared her a Doctor of the Church in 1970. Her lamp was full because she spent long hours with the Bridegroom in prayer; from that prayer came her fire for the Church. In one of her letters she wrote that if we are what we ought to be, we will set all Italy on fire (in substance). Ask her today for that fire, and for love of the Church and the Pope. Spend some time in prayer before the Most Holy Qurbono if you can: that is where the oil is given.
outline: Ask: if the Lord came tonight, would my lamp be burning?
The wise and foolish bridesmaids; the oil that cannot be borrowed.
Spirit, soul and body made ready; the faithful God who will do it.
Point 3 · St Catherine, a burning lamp
Prayer that became fire for the Church.
“The one who calls you is faithful, and he will do this.”
live: Spend fifteen minutes today in quiet prayer, before the Blessed Sacrament if you can, or at home before an icon.
Ask someone to pray for you this week, and pray daily for the Pope and our bishops, as St Catherine did.
2027-04-29.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, risen Bridegroom of the Church, you will come at an hour we do not know. Keep our lamps burning with the oil of your love, so that when the cry goes up at midnight we may go out to meet you and enter the wedding banquet with joy. God of peace, sanctify us entirely, spirit, soul and body, for you who call us are faithful. By the prayers of St Catherine of Siena, who spent herself in prayer and in love for your Church, kindle in us her fire, and bless our Holy Father the Pope and all the shepherds of your flock. You live and reign for ever. Amen.
altar: The Bridegroom has already come to meet us: in the Holy Qurbono the risen Christ gives himself to his bride the Church, and fills our lamps with the oil of his love.

quick: Five bridesmaids took oil with their lamps and five did not; only those who were ready went in to the wedding banquet.
Paul prays that the God of peace may sanctify us entirely, spirit, soul and body: the one who calls us is faithful.
St Catherine of Siena (1347–1380), Doctor of the Church, burned with prayer and love for the Church and the Pope.
2027-04-29.action: Spend fifteen minutes in quiet prayer today, before the Blessed Sacrament if possible.
2027-04-29.question: What is the oil I need to buy now, before the Bridegroom comes?

family.explain: Ten girls were waiting with lamps for a bridegroom so that they could go to the wedding party. Five brought extra oil, and five did not. The bridegroom came late at night. The girls without oil had to go and buy some, and when they came back the door was shut. Jesus wants us always to be ready for him. We fill our lamps with love when we pray, go to church and are kind to others. St Catherine of Siena was a girl who loved Jesus so much that her lamp was always full.
family.intention: We pray for the Pope and for the whole Church, as St Catherine did.
family.ask: Ask: “What can each of us do this week to keep our lamp full of love?”

illus: A nurse from Kottayam working night shifts in a hospital in the Gulf kept a small oil lamp on the shelf of her shared room. She could not light it there, so she kept it unlit and said a short prayer every time she looked at it: Lord, keep my lamp full. Her roommates, of other faiths, sometimes asked about it. One night, after a patient she had cared for for weeks died on her shift, she came home exhausted and sat on her bed in tears. One of her roommates quietly took the little lamp down from the shelf and put it in her hands, saying: you told me this is for when you are empty. They sat together till dawn. The nurse said later that it was the first time she had understood that the oil was not her own strength.

pm.open: Christ is risen! Lord Jesus, risen Bridegroom, keep our lamps burning until you come. Amen.
share: The wise took flasks of oil with their lamps (Matthew 25:4). What is the oil in my life, and is it running low?
May the God of peace himself sanctify you entirely (1 Thessalonians 5:23). Which part of my life have I kept back from God's holiness?
Beloved, pray for us (1 Thessalonians 5:25). Whom do I need to ask for prayer, and for whom must I pray?
interc: For the Church throughout the world, that she may be a bride ready for her Lord.
For the Pope and all bishops, that St Catherine's prayers may give them courage and wisdom.
For women who give their lives in prayer and service, especially consecrated women.
For nurses and all who care for the sick through the night.
For those whose lamps of faith are going out, that the faithful God may renew them.
pm.close: Father, your Son is the Bridegroom who will come at midnight. By the prayers of St Catherine of Siena, fill us with the oil of love, sanctify us entirely, and keep us awake and ready to enter the banquet of the Lamb. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, Christ is risen! Jesus tells of ten bridesmaids waiting with lamps for the bridegroom. Five of them were foolish, and five were wise. The wise took flasks of oil with their lamps (Matthew 25:2–4). At midnight the cry goes up: look! Here is the bridegroom! Come out to meet him (Matthew 25:6).

Those who were ready went in to the wedding banquet, and the door was shut (Matthew 25:10). The oil cannot be borrowed at the last moment. St Augustine said it is the oil of love. Keep awake therefore, for you know neither the day nor the hour (Matthew 25:13).

Paul prays: may the God of peace himself sanctify you entirely; and may your spirit and soul and body be kept sound and blameless at the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ. And he encourages us: the one who calls you is faithful, and he will do this (1 Thessalonians 5:23–24). God gives the oil, if we keep coming to him.

St Catherine of Siena, whom we remember today, was a wise virgin. A dyer's daughter with little schooling, she prayed so deeply that she became a Doctor of the Church, and she loved the Church so much that she persuaded the Pope to return to Rome. Let us ask her prayers, fill our lamps in prayer and at the Qurbono, and be ready for the Bridegroom. Amen.
kids: Children, Christ is risen! Jesus told a story about ten girls waiting for a wedding with their lamps. Five brought extra oil and five forgot. When the bridegroom came at midnight, only the girls with oil could go to the party! Jesus wants our hearts to be like lamps full of oil, ready for him. We fill them when we pray and love others. Today we remember St Catherine, a girl from Italy who prayed every day and loved Jesus with all her heart. Ask her to help you pray too!

intro: Theme: “The one who calls you is faithful, and he will do this.”
On Thursday of the fourth week after Qyomtho, with St Catherine of Siena: oil in the lamps, the whole person made holy, and a saint on fire for the Church.

sub: The oil that cannot be borrowed.
q: Your word is a lamp to my feet and a light to my path.
In the same way, let your light shine before others, so that they may see your good works and give glory to your Father in heaven.
points.apply: Spend fifteen minutes today in quiet prayer, and let it become a daily habit until Pentecost.

sub: The faithful God who will do it.
q: A new heart I will give you, and a new spirit I will put within you; and I will remove from your body the heart of stone and give you a heart of flesh.
I appeal to you therefore, brothers and sisters, by the mercies of God, to present your bodies as a living sacrifice, holy and acceptable to God, which is your spiritual worship.
points.apply: Offer one bodily discipline to God this week: an early rising for prayer, a fast from screens, a visit to the sick.

sub: The risen Christ, Bridegroom of the Church.
q: and as the bridegroom rejoices over the bride, so shall your God rejoice over you.
Blessed are those who are invited to the marriage supper of the Lamb.
points.apply: Pray each day this week for the Pope and our bishops, as St Catherine did.

concl: The oil of love is filled in prayer and cannot be borrowed at the last hour.
St Catherine's burning lamp became fire for the whole Church; the faithful God can do the same in us.
2027-04-29.resolve: Fill your lamp in prayer, offer God your whole self, and stay ready for the Bridegroom.
